**Safe sync procedure (GitHub main → tangled main):**
1. `git fetch origin main` → `TANGLED=$(git rev-parse origin/main)`
2. `git fetch git@mal.github.com:malpercio-dev/ezpds.git main` → `GITHUB=$(git rev-parse FETCH_HEAD)` (GitHub isn't a named fetch remote — fetch by URL into FETCH_HEAD)
3. Guard: push ONLY if `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$TANGLED" "$GITHUB"` (clean fast-forward; tangled has no divergent commits). If diverged, STOP and report.
4. `git merge --ff-only "$GITHUB"` on local `main`, then `git push git@knot.malpercio.dev:malpercio.dev/ezpds main` (push the **tangled URL only**, not `origin`, to avoid the dual-push round-trip to GitHub).

**Why it matters:** pushing tangled `main` triggers tangled's `staging.yaml` → `just ci-pds` gate → **Railway staging deploy**. Production is never touched by `main` — only a `v*` tag promotes to prod. Pre-validate locally with `just ci-pds` + `cargo build --release --locked -p pds` (the deploy's exact build). (Recipe was `ci-relay`/`relay` until the relay→pds crate rename landed on canonical main 2026-06-27.)

**When tangled has DIVERGED (not a clean fast-forward) — reconcile by overwriting, GitHub wins:** This happens when tangled `main` carries local commits GitHub lacks (e.g. a stale dead-end branch was once pushed to tangled). The `sync-tangled-main` recipe correctly REFUSES (the `merge-base --is-ancestor` guard) and says "reconcile manually." Do NOT try to `git rebase` tangled's commits onto GitHub (or GitHub's onto tangled) — if both sides independently did a big refactor (e.g. relay→pds rename) every file conflicts as "both added/both deleted" and you get a 50-commit conflict slog. A clean `git rebase --abort` always bails you out of a mid-conflict rebase with zero loss (orig-head = where you started). Recovered exactly this on 2026-06-27.

**When tangled has DIVERGED but its unique commit is LEGITIMATE (GitHub lacks real work) — cherry-pick onto GitHub, GitHub stays canonical:** Distinct from the "redundant divergence, overwrite" case above. Happens when someone commits directly to tangled `main` (bypassing the GitHub PR flow) — e.g. `chore: ignore llm-wiki` committed to tangled main and pushed there only. Here `git diff <github> <tangled>` shows tangled holds *unique content GitHub doesn't have*, so you must NOT `reset --hard` tangled away (that drops the work). The cherry-pick gives the work a NEW SHA, so the original tangled commit can never be an ancestor of GitHub — a force-push to tangled is unavoidable, but it's safe because the content is preserved on GitHub.

**Gotcha — `--force-with-lease` to a bare URL fails with "stale info":** the bare lease compares against the remote-*tracking* ref (`refs/remotes/origin/main`), but a push to a URL (not the named remote) has no tracking ref to lease against, so git rejects blind. Fix: pass the explicit expected value — `git push --force-with-lease=main:<current-tangled-sha> git@knot.malpercio.dev:malpercio.dev/ezpds main`. (`<current-tangled-sha>` = what `origin/main` / `FETCH_HEAD` says tangled is now.) If it STILL says stale info with the explicit SHA, tangled genuinely moved — stop and re-check.

**Gotcha — after a URL push, `git status` shows phantom "diverged" forever:** pushing to a URL and the recipe's `git fetch <url> main` (lands in `FETCH_HEAD`) never update `refs/remotes/origin/main`, so the cached ref stays at the old SHA and git keeps reporting divergence even though the remotes match. Fix: `git fetch origin` (canonical), or — if you've already proven the remote's SHA via `FETCH_HEAD` — `git update-ref refs/remotes/origin/main <sha>` (instant, no network).

**Gotcha:** the shell here is **zsh**, where `${PIPESTATUS[0]}` is empty — to capture a piped command's real exit, wrap in `bash -c '... | tail; echo EXIT=${PIPESTATUS[0]}'`, else the harness reports the trailing echo's exit, not the command's. Both tasks are done. Here's the summary.

## ✅ 1. Stale branch cleanup
Deleted **95 stale branches** from the Tangled knot (every branch present on Tangled but absent from GitHub — agent `claude/*`, issue `malpercio/mm-*`, and old `release/*` branches). The knot now holds exactly the canonical set:

```
main
production
entire/checkpoints/v1
```

## ✅ 2. Main-only mirroring — remotes split
The dual-pushurl `origin` (the reason feature branches leaked to the knot) is split into two remotes:

| Remote | URL | Push behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `origin` | GitHub | fetch + push, **all** branches |
| `tangled` | knot | push-only, **`refs/heads/main:refs/heads/main`** + `--no-tags` |

Verified by dry-run: a bare **`git push tangled` now pushes only `main`**, and feature-branch pushes to `origin` no longer touch the knot.

### Your new workflow
- Feature work: `git push origin <branch>` → GitHub only, as before.
- Sync the mirror after a merge to main:
```bash
git push tangled
```

## Two notes
- **`entire/checkpoints/v1`** will keep appearing on the knot — the `entire` plugin pushes it via its own hook on every `git push`, independent of the refspec. That's a durable checkpoint branch, not pollution, so I left it.
- **`production` on the knot** is now an unmaintained copy (the refspec only mirrors `main`, and Railway prod watches GitHub's `production` branch, not the knot). If you want a *strict* main-only mirror, say the word and I'll delete it from the knot too:
```bash
git push tangled --delete production
```

I also updated the sync memory doc, since the old dual-pushurl topology it described no longer exists.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
The lasting fix wasn't a config flag — it was recognizing that **refspecs are per-remote, not per-URL**. Any "different rules for different destinations" mirroring requirement forces a remote split. The dual-pushurl trick is only ever appropriate when you want the *exact same* refs at every destination.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
